title: Grateful Dead Live at Red Rocks Amphitheatre on 1982-07-27
lineage: FOB - Senn 421's> Sony TC-D5 (at mouth of the stage)> Nak Dragon Playback> HHB CDR-850 (no DAT gen)> CDR

ai_review.summary: High‑energy Red Rocks ’82 show with smoking China>Rider and a monster Playin' > Terrapin sequence captured on vivid audience tape.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its relentless energy, especially the blazing China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider stretch and the epic Playin' → Terrapin sandwich that leads into a powerful Other One.  While the audience recording isn’t pristine—some mic‑placement quirks and level jumps are noted—it benefits from Red Rocks’ natural acoustics, delivering bright Jerry guitar and full Phil bass.  Overall the show is considered one of the standout early‑80s runs at the venue.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 4‑5) and enthusiastic comments about both performance and tape quality; weighting favors a strong show with good but not flawless recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Bright front‑mic on Garcia, occasional mic fiddling (e.g., On the Road Again) and level jumps; overall clear and upfront sound that benefits from Red Rocks acoustics.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Playing in the Band > Terrapin Station
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set rolls solidly with tight tempos; second set kicks off with an unusual Playin' start and builds through Terrapin, The Other One and a soaring Stella Blue before a brief encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Front‑mic makes his guitar especially bright; tone praised throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass sounds fuller; notable “Phil bombs” on The Other One and aggressive slap technique highlighted.
band_member_comments.Bob: Scat vocal during Playing in the Band noted as a rare highlight; sweet solo on Roses appreciated.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent's organ drives Terrapin, adding intensity; overall keyboard presence felt strong despite occasional mix quirks.
band_member_comments.Drums: Thrilling drum break leading into Rhythm Devils shout‑out; drums praised for driving the high‑energy jams.
